CAR-T QSP Model — Layer 3 Sensitivity & Identifiability (v2)

Log-transformed metrics on a moderate-response baseline

2026-06-07

1 Why this v2

The v1 sensitivity analysis produced nonsensically large elasticities (n_mono at ~3600, other kinetic parameters in the hundreds), and flagged almost every parameter pair as “unidentifiable” including combinations with no shared mechanism (e.g., k_growth vs Kd_sBCMA at |cor| = 0.96).

Root cause: the v1 baseline theta sat in a strong-response regime where tumor cleared to ~2.6e+04 cells by day 365 and nadir_sBCMA hit exactly 0. At these near-zero baselines, the elasticity formula (ΔM/M)/(Δp/p) blows up and every kinetic parameter’s sensitivity vector ends up dominated by “distance to the clearance cliff.” The correlation matrix then measures proximity to the cliff rather than each parameter’s distinctive mechanistic fingerprint.

Two fixes in this version:

  1. Moderate-response baseline. Vmax_mono reduced from 0.8 to 0.3 so the low-antigen clone persists meaningfully. k_growth reduced from 1.2 to 0.9 so peak expansion lands closer to the clinical 7–21 day window.

  2. Log-transformed metrics with floors. All metrics spanning many orders of magnitude are log10(M + floor) before differencing. The collapsing nadir_sBCMA is replaced by sBCMA_AUC60 (integrated exposure over first 60 days), which is robustly non-zero. The sensitivity formula becomes the clean log-log elasticity d log10(M) / d log10(p).

2 Model (unchanged from earlier layers)

3 Moderate-response baseline

3.1 Baseline sanity check

Before running sensitivity, confirm the baseline is in a moderate regime: CAR-T peak in a realistic window, tumor neither cleared nor uncontrolled, sBCMA meaningfully non-zero.

## Baseline summary:
##   Peak E at day:      25   (want 7-21)
##   Peak E magnitude:   3.86e+11
##   Tumor at day 90:    3.94e+09
##   Tumor at day 365:   4.47e+11   (want 10^7 - 10^11)
##   Peak sBCMA:         9.94
##   sBCMA at day 30:    0.063

If tumor_day365 is < 10⁵ or > 10¹¹, the baseline is still at an extreme and Vmax_mono needs further adjustment. The sensitivity analysis below is only as trustworthy as this baseline.

4 Summary metrics (log-transformed)

Eight scalar summaries corresponding to clinical observables. All log-transformed with floors so they behave well under any perturbation.

##       log_peak_E     log_t_peak_E     log_AUC_E_28     log_E_day180 
##            11.59             1.40            12.71             3.62 
##  log_tumor_day90 log_tumor_day365  log_sBCMA_AUC60  log_sBCMA_day30 
##             9.60            11.65             1.54            -1.20

Every metric should be non-degenerate (not at floor). If any are, the baseline needs further adjustment before the sensitivity results carry meaning.

5 Local sensitivity analysis

5.1 Parameter selection

Same 16 parameters as v1: kinetic and pharmacological parameters, with antigen densities, K_max, and redundant shed rates excluded.

5.2 Log-log sensitivity coefficients

For each parameter, perturb by ±10% and compute

\[ S_{ij} = \frac{\Delta \log_{10} M_j}{\Delta \log_{10} p_i} \]

This is the dimensionless log-log elasticity. Interpretation: S = 1 means “a factor-of-2 change in parameter produces a factor-of-2 change in metric.” Values around 0 mean no effect; typical informative values are in the 0.1–5 range. Unlike the v1 linear-elasticity formula, this stays well-behaved even when metric values are tiny because the log transform absorbs the dynamic range.

7.2 Correlation heatmap

8 Recommendations for nlmixr2 fit

Apply these filters after reviewing the output above — they’re guidance, not a hard rule.

8.1 Fix to literature values

Parameters with total_abs < 1 (essentially no signal across any observed metric at this baseline). Estimating these adds degrees of freedom without data to support them.

Parameters with max_abs < 0.3 (no single metric moves much) are also fix candidates even if total_abs is moderate across many weak effects.

8.2 Estimate as typical value only (no BSV)

Moderate signal (max_abs between 0.3 and 1, n_significant ≥ 2) but strongly correlated (|cor| > 0.85) with another estimated parameter. Or: parameters where between-subject variability would be over-parameterization given typical sparse sampling.

8.3 Estimate with BSV (typical value + random effect)

Parameters meeting both:

  • Strong signal: max_abs > 1 in at least one metric
  • Independent: |cor| < 0.85 with every other estimated parameter

8.4 Reparameterize correlated pairs

Common patterns for this model:

  • frac_mem ↔︎ k_decay_mem. These combine linearly in decay_rate. Fix frac_mem to a literature value (e.g., 0.15) and estimate k_decay_eff and k_decay_mem separately, or collapse to a single effective decay rate.
  • Hill triplets (Vmax, EC50, n). At a single antigen density, these are not separately identifiable. Fix n to a literature value (usually 1 or 2) and estimate Vmax and EC50. If you have multiple patients with different antigen densities, all three can be estimated jointly; at a single density, drop one.

8.5 Staged fitting order

  1. Stage 1 — PK alone. Fit k_growth, k_decay_eff, k_ld_recover on CAR_obs only. Fix PD.
  2. Stage 2 — PD on top. With stage-1 estimates fixed, fit Vmax_mono, EC50_mono (and Vmax_bival if the data has high-antigen patients with enough response variability) on tumor and CAR data jointly.
  3. Stage 3 — sBCMA. With PK/PD fixed, fit k_shed_high, k_clear_sBCMA on sBCMA data.
  4. Stage 4 — joint refinement. Release everything, use stage 1–3 estimates as initial values, and run a final joint SAEM.
